proof_encoding: RPA 5, one JSON line: {'claims':[4],'blocks':[4]}; the two forward blocks are plain Return over the 5,826 output map in target order with 25,123 (integer) / 22,656 (relaxed) ordered check refs; the two reverse blocks are End.IntervalLift with 2,467 intervals and a body Return of 67,992 / 65,525 refs.

Per interval the payload is lower=[a*y, t+b*(1-y)], upper=[M*y, t+c*(1-y)] and exactly 4 premise refs in lower-major order, proved by (M-a)*lower(y), target row rg, target row rl, (c-b)*upper(y); those refs are Lin steps proved in the parent-scope prelude (4,865 steps) before the endpoint.

The reverse body runs on a hand-built mirror of the kernel's extension: 2,467 free coordinates z_k at index N+k, then per interval every lower row and every upper row (9,868 rows per claim); the body maps source v->z_k, w->z_k-t_k, fixed zeros->0 and re-proves all 10,112 source rows.

request.json (1,061,036 B) is four copies of one claim record: 3,359 [input,output] coordinate pairs plus 2,467 (input Expr, output Expr) affine observations, written byte-identically from the same Python objects (tools/prepare_test23.py:135).

Negative proofs: four mutated certificates (a missing middle compatibility pair on interval 1234, a changed lower bound, w=z+t instead of w=z-t, an altered requested observation) assemble and then verify as INVALID with exit 2.

Reconstructed the entire block structure by exhaustive scans: 2,467 binaries each with exactly 4 constraint occurrences over a disjoint pair of continuous columns, 16,500 fixed zeros, opposite equality columns in every equality, and pair coverage of all 9,868 inequalities.

Built the signed equality graph over the 244 equalities, propagated +/-1 row weights to a conflict-free assignment (183 at +1, 61 at -1), verified the exact zero-row and zero-RHS identity, and selected c1 as the removed row.

Proved the difference-of-intervals projection by hand and ran 37,005 exact lift checks at y in {0,1/4,1/2,3/4,1} with endpoint/midpoint choices, plus the integer lift v=max(t,0), w=max(-t,0) and the max(a*y, t+b*(1-y)) relaxation lift.

Hand-wrote the MPS writer with exact terminating decimals, audit.json (988,778 B) with per-pair parameters/rows/lifts and hashes, and a 184-line verify.py that rebuilds the edit from the certificate and compares every parsed field of the artifact.

friction: No public proof-construction API, so the preparer re-codes the kernel's own extension layout (coordinate index N+k, lower-then-upper row order, fresh names) in Python purely to obtain handles; any drift surfaces only as an opaque INVALID, never as a build error.

Every premise reference must be a fact for exactly LE(lower[i]-upper[j]), so the preparer needs its own three-way dispatch, and a count or order error is reported only as 'INVALID interval: missing or surplus lower-upper pair checks' with no item index.

Failure reports do not identify the witness item: the missing-middle mutant removes intervals[1234].checks[2] and the report names neither item 1234 nor premise 2, and another mutant reports only 'obligation 1956'.

The structural facts (2,467 pairs with a/M/b/c, deleted rows/columns, 244 dependency weights) live in the analyst's audit.json and are re-asserted by a second 104-line implementation just before emission, duplicating every check the compiler will need.

Both directions require hand-derived terms per obligation: forward target rows are built as source-row combinations rg+sl and rl+sg (:88-89) and reverse rows from generated rows plus the 243-term equality combination (:118-120), with nothing deriving them from the edit.

top_capability: RULE_BUILDERS - typed IntervalLift/SignedLift constructors that materialise the joint extension and hand back generated coordinate and row references. This certificate is one 2,467-interval IntervalLift per reverse claim whose body must address kernel-generated rows by index, and the sign-split family's preconditions (V8 forces F=0 when Z=0) decide which rule can express a block at all.
notes: Family note for the aggregator: test23 is the V5 interval case of the sign-split family (audit/draft_review.md:91 groups test23/test27/test30). grep over cases/test23/proof.rpa gives 0 SignedLift and 2 IntervalLift (receipt interval_lifts=2), so the delivered per-decomposition payload is the V5 interval one, not a V8 SignedWitness; the V8 signed decomposition cannot express these blocks because a Signed item forces F=0 whenever Z=0 (docs/FORMAT_V8.md), while each pair's integer projection is the separated set [-c,-b] union [a,M] (digest report, hypothesis 8: nonzero forbidden gap), which is why the activation y is retained and the two identity rows of the target are re-proved. Design consequence: one joint extension of 2,467 intervals is required (nested per-pair lifts would exceed the depth-64 budget [INFERENCE]), and a compiler must pick the rule family by checked preconditions, not by the finding's prose. Scale: RPA 16,794,987 B = 6.3% of the 256 MiB text budget, RPX 11,850,424 B, request 1,061,036 B; verification executed in 17.46 s of a 19.07 s run.
